connect-protocol-version.description: Define the version of the Connect protocol

code.description: The status code, which should be an enum value of [google.rpc.Code][google.rpc.Code].

message.description: A developer-facing error message, which should be in English. Any user-facing error message should be localized and sent in the [google.rpc.Status.details][google.rpc.Status.details] field, or localized by the client.

details.description: A list of messages that carry the error details. There is no limit on the number of messages.

type.description: A URL that acts as a globally unique identifier for the type of the serialized message. For example: `type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.ErrorInfo`.

value.description: The Protobuf message, serialized as bytes and base64-encoded. The specific message type is identified by the `type` field.

debug.title: Debug
debug.description: Deserialized error detail payload. The 'type' field indicates the schema. This field is for easier debugging and should not be relied upon for application logic.

connect.error_details.Any.description: Contains an arbitrary serialized message along with a @type that describes the type of the serialized message, with an additional debug field for ConnectRPC error details.

google.protobuf.Duration.description: A signed duration in seconds, with up to nine fractional digits and an `s` suffix (for example, `3s` or `-0.001s`).

google.protobuf.FieldMask.description: Comma-separated field paths in lowerCamelCase (for example, `user.displayName,photo`).

google.protobuf.ListValue.description: A JSON array whose elements may be any JSON value.

google.protobuf.NullValue.title: NullValue
google.protobuf.NullValue.description:
Represents a JSON `null`.

 `NullValue` is a sentinel, using an enum with only one value to represent
 the null value for the `Value` type union.

 A field of type `NullValue` with any value other than `0` is considered
 invalid. Most ProtoJSON serializers will emit a Value with a `null_value` set
 as a JSON `null` regardless of the integer value, and so will round trip to
 a `0` value.

- `NULL_VALUE`: Null value.
x-enum-descriptions: Null value.

google.protobuf.Struct.description: A JSON object whose property values may be any JSON value.

google.protobuf.Timestamp.description: A point in time in RFC 3339 format, with up to nanosecond precision. Output uses UTC (`Z`); input may use an offset from UTC.

google.protobuf.Value.description: Any JSON value: `null`, number, string, boolean, array, or object.

spin.v1.AccessPerson.title: AccessPerson
spin.v1.AccessPerson.description:
AccessPerson is somebody an access names: a user, and their keyring by the version it began at
 (ownerword.Person). name is how the dashboard shows them, and no part of what is signed.

spin.v1.AllowedEmailType.title: AllowedEmailType
spin.v1.AllowedEmailType.description:
Allowed email type enum

- `ALLOWED_EMAIL_TYPE_EMAIL`: Exact email address match
- `ALLOWED_EMAIL_TYPE_DOMAIN`: Domain suffix match (@domain.com)
x-enum-descriptions: Exact email address match
Domain suffix match (@domain.com)

callbackUrl.title: callback_url
callbackUrl.description: The workspace host's callback with the one-time code, for the browser to be sent to.

publish.title: publish
publish.description:
publish tries a publish of commit again when the last one failed; without it, that
 failure is the answer. A client sets it on its first ask, and not on those that follow.

spin.v1.AttachVSCodeServerRequest.title: AttachVSCodeServerRequest
spin.v1.AttachVSCodeServerRequest.description:
AttachVSCodeServerRequest names the server a VS Code client runs: the second line of its
 `code --version`. A publish takes minutes, far past a request, so the answer is where it
 stands, and a client asks again until the server is attached.

attached.title: attached
attached.description:
attached: the workspace has the server now. Otherwise it is being published, and step says
 where that is.

detached.title: detached
detached.description: detached are the servers the workspace gave up to make room, asked for longest ago.

actorId.title: actor_id
actorId.description:
actor_id is empty for an operation nobody was signed in for - a failed login, a runner
 registering itself - and for one whose user has since been deleted.

actorEmail.title: actor_email
actorEmail.description:
actor_email is empty for the same reasons, and is what the user's row says now rather
 than what it said then.

resourceId.title: resource_id
resourceId.description:
resource_id is empty for an operation with no row to point at - a failed login, a
 change to the installation's settings. resource_type still says what kind of thing it
 was about.

details.title: details
details.description:
details is the JSON the operation recorded, verbatim. It has no schema: what a login
 records and what a team membership change records have nothing in common, and a reader
 that insists on a shape would have to be changed by every new action.

spin.v1.AuditEntry.title: AuditEntry
spin.v1.AuditEntry.description:
AuditEntry is one recorded operation, as it was recorded: the log is append-only and
 nothing here is derived at read time except the actor's email, which is joined so a
 reader is not handed a UUID to look up by hand.

version.title: version
version.description: The machine release it was taken from.

clones.title: clones
clones.description: How many volumes were cloned from it: every workspace disk that began as it, and still is.

untagged.title: untagged
untagged.description: Its ref was taken off it: no new workspace gets it, the disks cloned from it go on reading it.

given.title: given
given.description: What a workspace that names no image is given now.

pinned.title: pinned
pinned.description: The one this control plane's release pins; given once it is published.

volumeId.title: volume_id
volumeId.description: Its volume in the store, which RemoveStoredVolume takes when removable.

removable.title: removable
removable.description:
No disk was cloned from it and it is not the one given: RemoveStoredVolume untags it on the
 way and removes it.

spin.v1.BaseImage.title: BaseImage
spin.v1.BaseImage.description: BaseImage is the base image of one machine release, as published.

host.title: host
host.description:
The workspace's host the browser asked for, as the proxy received it: <name>.ws.<domain>.
 The code comes back to this host and to no other.

returnPath.title: return_path
returnPath.description: Where on that host the browser goes once it is signed in: a path, never a URL.

approveUrl.title: approve_url
approveUrl.description: The dashboard's page that approves this sign-in, for the browser to be sent to.

binding.title: binding
binding.description:
A secret for the browser that began this sign-in, kept where only the proxy reads it:
 CompleteWorkspaceSignIn requires it with the code, so a code opened in another browser -
 one somebody was sent a link to - signs nobody in.

path.title: path
path.description: As the machine sent it, without the query.

status.title: status
status.description: What the real host answered; what the proxy answered for a refusal.

refused.title: refused
refused.description:
Empty for a request passed on. Otherwise why the proxy refused it: credentials (a secret or
 token the team does not hold), host (a request for another name), upgrade, method (TRACE or
 TRACK), scope (a method or path the injecting rule does not allow), authority (the cloud
 principal refused to sign it).

principal.title: principal
principal.description: Who asked: "user" or "agent", by the listener the proxy read it on.

spin.v1.BrokeredRequest.title: BrokeredRequest
spin.v1.BrokeredRequest.description:
BrokeredRequest is one request the egress proxy read from the workspace's machine to a brokered
 name. No header and no body: what the proxy set is the team's secret, and what the machine
 sent is its own.

spin.v1.BurstMode.title: BurstMode
spin.v1.BurstMode.description:
BurstMode is how a workspace of a preset may grow past what it starts with.

- `BURST_MODE_FIXED`: FIXED starts at the preset's size and stays there.
- `BURST_MODE_TO_PRESET`: TO_PRESET starts at the preset's burst floor and may grow to its size.
- `BURST_MODE_TO_HOST`: TO_HOST starts at the preset's burst floor and may grow to everything its host has.
x-enum-descriptions: FIXED starts at the preset's size and stays there.
TO_PRESET starts at the preset's burst floor and may grow to its size.
TO_HOST starts at the preset's burst floor and may grow to everything its host has.

user.title: user
user.description: Only set when status is DEVICE_LOGIN_STATUS_COMPLETE

sessionToken.title: session_token
sessionToken.description:
The session token as the proxy received it, empty for a request with no session at all.
 Only a PUBLIC port is reachable that way.

spin.v1.CheckPortAccessRequest.title: CheckPortAccessRequest
spin.v1.CheckPortAccessRequest.description:
Whether one request may reach one published port.

 This is the gate in front of a workspace's published ports, and it lives in the control
 plane rather than in the proxy because the levels only mean something if the party that
 decides also holds the facts. The proxy forwards the browser's session token and the
 control plane *validates* it - it does not take a user id the proxy asserts, which would
 make the proxy's word the credential.

access.title: access
access.description:
What the port's level is, so the proxy can tell a refusal that a login would fix from
 one it would not: an anonymous request to a PRIVATE port is a redirect, and a signed-in
 request to the same port is a 403 no amount of signing in changes.

workspaceId.title: workspace_id
workspaceId.description:
The workspace the name was decided about, when allowed. The proxy pools connections by
 it and opens sessions for it: a name is freed by a rename and taken by someone else's
 workspace, and a connection pooled by name would carry the next request into the old one.

spin.v1.CheckPortPublishedRequest.title: CheckPortPublishedRequest
spin.v1.CheckPortPublishedRequest.description:
Whether a certificate may be obtained for one workspace port's hostname.

 Not CheckPortAccess with no session: that asks whether an anonymous request may reach the
 port, and the answer is no for every PRIVATE and WHITELIST port, and for every PUBLIC one while
 the installation keeps ports closed to everybody - each of them a name with no certificate,
 and so no handshake for the owner or a grantee to sign in over. A certificate is for the name,
 so the question is whether the name is published at all.

published.title: published
published.description: The port is published on a workspace that is not deleted, at any level and in any state.

name.title: name
name.description: The clone's name; generated when empty.

snapshot.title: snapshot
snapshot.description: The source's snapshot the clone was made from, which stays as the clone's floor.

cloud.title: cloud
cloud.description:
The cloud: "aws", whose principal is an IAM role's ARN and whose requests are signed with
 SigV4.

spin.v1.CloudAccess.title: CloudAccess
spin.v1.CloudAccess.description: CloudAccess is a principal on a cloud a brokered rule's requests are authorized as.

binding.title: binding
binding.description: BeginWorkspaceSignInResponse.binding, as the browser presented it.

host.title: host
host.description: The host the callback arrived on, which must be the one the sign-in began on.

fileSays.title: file_says
fileSays.description:
What the file says, as a person reads it; empty where the file no longer declares the item,
 and applying the change removes it.

installationHas.title: installation_has
installationHas.description: What the installation has, the same way; empty where it has none.

says.title: says
says.description:
The file's declaration this change is about, sent back as it came: a decision about one the
 file has changed since is refused rather than taken as about the newer one.

since.title: since
since.description: When the file started saying it.

spin.v1.ConfigChange.title: ConfigChange
spin.v1.ConfigChange.description: One thing the config file says differently from the installation.

spin.v1.ConfigItemKind.title: ConfigItemKind
spin.v1.ConfigItemKind.description:
What one item of the installation's config file is.

- `CONFIG_ITEM_KIND_SETTING`: A setting, by its key: registration_mode, default_network_tags, allowed_images...
- `CONFIG_ITEM_KIND_EMAIL`: An address or domain registration admits, by itself.
x-enum-descriptions: A setting, by its key: registration_mode, default_network_tags, allowed_images...
An address or domain registration admits, by itself.

callbackUrl.title: callback_url
callbackUrl.description: The callback URL to configure in GitHub OAuth app settings

userCode.title: user_code
userCode.description: The user code entered by the user (e.g., "ABCD-1234")

slug.title: slug
slug.description: Made from the name when empty

teamId.title: team_id
teamId.description: Optional: scope to team (host joins team's pool)

reusable.title: reusable
reusable.description:
A pool's token, for an autoscaling group whose machines register with nobody at them: it
 is not spent by the host it registers. Short-lived and rotated is the intended use.

hostPolicy.title: host_policy
hostPolicy.description:
The policy each host it registers starts with, under SetHostPolicy's rules; host_id must
 be empty, since the hosts do not exist yet.

burstFloorCpuCores.title: burst_floor_cpu_cores
burstFloorCpuCores.description: Required for a burst mode: what its workspaces start with, at most the preset's size.

bandwidthMbps.title: bandwidth_mbps
bandwidthMbps.description: What a workspace of it may carry each way, in megabits a second; 0 is unshaped.

rpoSeconds.title: rpo_seconds
rpoSeconds.description:
How far behind the object store a workspace of it may fall, in seconds; 0 is the
 installation's.

withMemory.title: with_memory
withMemory.description:
with_memory keeps the machine's memory too, taken at the instant the disk is sealed; the
 guest is paused for tens of milliseconds, and the call returns once the memory is written.

parentId.title: parent_id
parentId.description: Optional: parent team ID (empty = root team)

slug.title: slug
slug.description: Optional, generated from name if empty

teamId.title: team_id
teamId.description: Optional: team ID (personal workspace if empty)

image.title: image
image.description: A published image (ListImages); required unless from_snapshot_id is set

preset.title: preset
preset.description:
The preset it is sized by, by name (AdminService.ListResourcePresets): its cores, memory,
 disk and how it grows. Empty is the installation's default preset, or with none marked
 1 core, 512 MB and 10 GB free. A disabled preset is refused.

fromSnapshotId.title: from_snapshot_id
fromSnapshotId.description: Create workspace from a shared snapshot

networkTags.title: network_tags
networkTags.description:
network_tags are the network policies this workspace runs under, by name - the same
 idea as a GCP instance's network tags. The host's ruleset names the tag and holds the
 set of machines carrying it, so this decides which rules apply without naming a rule.

 Empty runs the workspace under the installation's default, and under "offline" where it
 declares none: a create that names nothing reaches nothing, rather than everything.
 A tag the host has no policy for fails the start rather than being ignored: a workspace
 asking for a policy the node does not have is a question with two answers, and quietly
 choosing "run it without" is how one ends up less contained than whoever launched it
 believes.

projectId.title: project_id
projectId.description:
A project of a team the caller is in: the workspace is the project's - its team, image,
 preset and tags, which the request then names none of - and its guest clones the project's
 repository at ref, the project's own when empty.

requestId.title: request_id
requestId.description:
Optional, at most 128 bytes: the client's key for this create, so a retry after an answer
 it never got is answered with the workspace the first attempt made. The same key with
 another request is refused (FAILED_PRECONDITION).

apply.title: apply
apply.description: True writes what the file says; false keeps what the installation has.

force.title: force
force.description: Force delete regardless of state (skips state validation)

permanently.title: permanently
permanently.description:
permanently erases the workspace now - its disk, snapshots and keys - rather than putting it
 in the trash; a workspace already in the trash is erased only this way. What is erased
 cannot be undeleted: the store expires its bytes when its retention ends.

trashedUntil.title: trashed_until
trashedUntil.description: Until when it can be undeleted; unset when it was erased.

name.title: name
name.description:
The name it had; another workspace may have taken it since, and an undelete then gives it
 another.

spin.v1.DeletedWorkspace.title: DeletedWorkspace
spin.v1.DeletedWorkspace.description: DeletedWorkspace is a workspace in the trash.

spin.v1.DeviceLoginStatus.title: DeviceLoginStatus
spin.v1.DeviceLoginStatus.description:
- `DEVICE_LOGIN_STATUS_PENDING`: User hasn't completed login yet
- `DEVICE_LOGIN_STATUS_COMPLETE`: Login complete, token available
- `DEVICE_LOGIN_STATUS_EXPIRED`: Device code expired
- `DEVICE_LOGIN_STATUS_DENIED`: User denied the request

Login complete, token available
Device code expired
User denied the request

fromSnapshotId.title: from_snapshot_id
fromSnapshotId.description: Empty compares from what the workspace was created from.

under.title: under
under.description:
under narrows the comparison to one path of the filesystem, from its root; empty is all of
 it. The walk starts there rather than filtering, so what is outside it costs nothing and
 does not fill the answer.

spin.v1.DiffSnapshotsRequest.title: DiffSnapshotsRequest
spin.v1.DiffSnapshotsRequest.description:
DiffSnapshotsRequest names two published snapshots of one workspace. The comparison runs in a
 machine of its own on a host of the control plane's choosing; the workspace need not be
 running, or on any host.

changes.title: changes
changes.description: Every change from one snapshot to the other, a directory before what is under it.

truncated.title: truncated
truncated.description: truncated says there are more changes than one answer carries.

suspend.title: suspend
suspend.description:
Suspend every running workspace off the host: its memory and disk go to the object store,
 and it is resumed on whichever other host has room, on its own - or, suspended without its
 memory, on its owner's next start. Answered once each is suspended or has failed to be; a
 workspace that failed runs on as it was.

leaveStopped.title: leave_stopped
leaveStopped.description:
leave_stopped is for a drain that shrinks the fleet: the workspaces it suspends stay stopped,
 and each resumes on another host when its owner starts it. Without it they are resumed
 elsewhere at once, waiting for a host where the installation is bringing one up.

what.title: what
what.description: What the object is, in words.

volume.title: volume
volume.description: Whose it is, when it is a volume's.

access.title: access
access.description: Left unset, this is PRIVATE. Exposing a port is not the same as publishing it.

httpsBackend.title: https_backend
httpsBackend.description:
The proxy speaks TLS to this port without verifying its certificate, and only under the
 {port}s- hostname: 3000-ws and 3000s-ws are different names, and one refuses.

grants.title: grants
grants.description:
Who this port is granted to, when access is WHITELIST. Output only, and populated only
 for the workspace's owner - who a port is shared with is the owner's business and not
 the grantees'.

version.title: version
version.description:
The release's own name: the control plane's version for the supervisor; for the VS Code
 servers, the versions it carries joined with +, unless it was named otherwise.

workspaces.title: workspaces
workspaces.description: How many workspaces run it; one that nothing runs and is not the newest is collectable.

newest.title: newest
newest.description: Whether a start is given this one.

spin.v1.ExtensionRelease.title: ExtensionRelease
spin.v1.ExtensionRelease.description: ExtensionRelease is one release of an extension: the supervisor, or the VS Code servers.

newest.title: newest
newest.description: Whether a start now would choose this release.

spin.v1.ExtensionVersion.title: ExtensionVersion
spin.v1.ExtensionVersion.description:
ExtensionVersion is a release and how many workspaces are on it: what an update leaves
 behind until each workspace is next started.

spin.v1.FieldValue.title: FieldValue
spin.v1.FieldValue.description: FieldValue is one value a field has, and how many of a search's records have it.

path.title: path
path.description:
From the filesystem's root, with a leading slash. A name holding bytes that are not UTF-8
 has them replaced here, and path_bytes holds the name as it is.

from.title: from
from.description: Unset on the side the path is not on.

spin.v1.FileChangeKind.title: FileChangeKind
spin.v1.FileChangeKind.description: - `FILE_CHANGE_KIND_MODIFIED`: The same type on both sides, and a different content, mode, owner or symlink target.
x-enum-descriptions: The same type on both sides, and a different content, mode, owner or symlink target.

mode.title: mode
mode.description: Permission bits, setuid, setgid and sticky included.

symlinkTarget.title: symlink_target
symlinkTarget.description: A symlink's target as stored, never followed; replaced and in symlink_target_bytes as path is.

sha256.title: sha256
sha256.description: A regular file's content hash in lowercase hex, where its content is what changed.

spin.v1.FileType.title: FileType
spin.v1.FileType.description: - `FILE_TYPE_OTHER`: A device, a FIFO or a socket.
x-enum-descriptions: A device, a FIFO or a socket.

machineVersion.title: machine_version
machineVersion.description: Empty on a host with no machine, such as the mock runner.

supported.title: supported
supported.description:
Whether this control plane serves a host of that version. An unsupported host is refused
 at its next registration, with note saying why.

spin.v1.FleetHostVersion.title: FleetHostVersion
spin.v1.FleetHostVersion.description: FleetHostVersion is one host's halves: the runner binary and the machine under it.

month.title: month
month.description: The month, as any instant in it (UTC's); unset is the month in progress.

readAt.title: read_at
readAt.description:
When the bill was last read; unset where it never was - no scope (bill_scope), or a cloud
 that sends none - and then nothing below is known.

currency.title: currency
currency.description: ISO 4217; every amount here is in millionths of it.

totalMicros.title: total_micros
totalMicros.description: The month so far, every day and service.

forecastMicros.title: forecast_micros
forecastMicros.description: What the month is forecast to end at; unset where the cloud has no forecast yet.

budgetLimitMicros.title: budget_limit_micros
budgetLimitMicros.description: The installation's budget and what the cloud counts against it; unset where it has none.

month.title: month
month.description: The month, as any instant in it (UTC's); unset is the month in progress.

currency.title: currency
currency.description: ISO 4217; every amount here is in millionths of it.

idleMicros.title: idle_micros
idleMicros.description: What the runners cost that no workspace held.

unstoredMicros.title: unstored_micros
unstoredMicros.description:
What the volumes' bucket cost for bytes no workspace keeps: the images, what nothing
 references any more.

platform.title: platform
platform.description: Every other cost - the control plane, the proxy, keys, logs - by service, costliest first.

controlPlaneVersion.title: control_plane_version
controlPlaneVersion.description:
The release of the control plane that answered, which is the release of the dashboard asking:
 the bundle is served from inside that binary. It rides here rather than on an endpoint of its
 own because every session asks this once, and because a version an installation will be
 matched against known flaws by is not something to hand out unauthenticated.

autoscaling.title: autoscaling
autoscaling.description:
False when no group is configured: the hosts of this installation are whatever somebody
 registered by hand, and none of the numbers below mean anything.

group.title: group
group.description: The group the control plane sizes, as its cloud names it.

desired.title: desired
desired.description:
What it last asked the group for, and the most it may ask: zero of one is a fleet at rest,
 which is what an idle installation looks like.

connected.title: connected
connected.description:
The hosts that are connected now, which lags desired by a machine's boot: one desired and
 none connected is a machine on its way.

waiting.title: waiting
waiting.description:
Workspaces that have nowhere to run yet, and when the first of them started waiting: this
 is what makes the control plane ask for a machine.

busy.title: busy
busy.description: Workspaces that are keeping the fleet up.

idleMinutes.title: idle_minutes
idleMinutes.description:
How long the fleet may be idle before the group is emptied, and the window in which it is
 emptied at once. Empty quiet_hours is none.

spin.v1.GetFleetResponse.title: GetFleetResponse
spin.v1.GetFleetResponse.description:
What an operator needs to read an empty list of hosts: whether the installation can bring one
 at all, how many it has asked for, and what is waiting. Every count is the control plane's own
 view now, not a stored one - a control plane that restarted starts counting again.

machineVersion.title: machine_version
machineVersion.description: The spin-machine release this control plane pins, which a host should be running.

writebackPresets.title: writeback_presets
writebackPresets.description:
The writeback thresholds an operator chooses from without testing them on the host, each
 with what it measured. The first is unset: what the host booted with.

writebackTest.title: writeback_test
writebackTest.description: The last writeback test of this host, while SetHostPolicy still takes its thresholds.

grafana.title: grafana
grafana.description:
Unset where the control plane serves none: the installation keeps no metrics, or this
 machine has no Grafana.

word.title: word
word.description: word is the newest the owner signed; unset for a workspace whose owner has signed none.

owner.title: owner
owner.description:
owner is the workspace's owner, with their keyring as it is now: who signs the next. Empty
 keyring for an owner who has signed none.

dotfiles.title: dotfiles
dotfiles.description:
settings are the startup configuration the guest would be handed at its next registration:
 the owner's settings after the team's policy. A word approves them by their digest, which
 the client computes from these, as the guest does from what it is handed.

egressRoot.title: egress_root
egressRoot.description:
egress_root is the installation's egress root, PEM: what the guest is handed at registration,
 and trusts only when a word names its digest. A client names it only once it has held it to
 the root it pinned for the installation, never on this answer's say alone.

identityAudiences.title: identity_audiences
identityAudiences.description:
identity_audiences is who the installation gives identities for, empty for anybody: what a
 client offers its owner to name in a word, which a host holds every token to as well.

teamId.title: team_id
teamId.description:
The workspace as its first access says it: team, image, and the snapshot and workspace it was
 cloned from. The next access says the same; the first says these.

guests.title: guests
guests.description:
guests are the people the owner invited, each with their keyring as it is now: who the next
 access names besides the owner. One with an empty keyring has signed none, and is named once
 they have.

role.title: role
role.description: role is the caller's: "owner", or "guest" - who reads it and signs nothing.

repository.title: repository
repository.description:
repository is the one the workspace opened, part of the settings a word approves as the
 five above are: unset for a workspace that opened no project.

prebuildClaim.title: prebuild_claim
prebuildClaim.description:
prebuild_claim is, for a workspace opened from a prebuild, the claim the host that built it
 signed (PrebuildClaim), whose SHA-256 repository.prebuild_claim_digest is: a client verifies
 it, and that it names the repository and the commit the settings do, before its word approves
 them.

prebuildWriters.title: prebuild_writers
prebuildWriters.description:
prebuild_writers is the record of the claim's writer, by its id (writers/<id>.json in the
 installation's store), which the client holds to its own anchors as it does a launch claim's.

images.title: images
images.description: Empty until the object store is configured: there is nowhere to publish to.

baseImages.title: base_images
baseImages.description: Every base image published, one per machine release, newest first.

supervisorReleases.title: supervisor_releases
supervisorReleases.description: Every release of the supervisor, newest first.

agentReleases.title: agent_releases
agentReleases.description: Every release of the agent CLIs (Claude Code and Codex, one extension), newest first.

needsSetup.title: needs_setup
needsSetup.description: True until the setup wizard has been completed: where the dashboard sends everybody.

hasOauth.title: has_oauth
hasOauth.description: True if any OAuth/OIDC provider is configured

setupCompleted.title: setup_completed
setupCompleted.description: True if setup wizard has been completed

forcePasswordChange.title: force_password_change
forcePasswordChange.description: True if current admin must change their password

hasBootstrapAdmin.title: has_bootstrap_admin
hasBootstrapAdmin.description: True if bootstrap admin is still active (should be disabled after OAuth setup)

hasStorage.title: has_storage
hasStorage.description: True if the object store is configured; until it is, no workspace can be created

signedIn.title: signed_in
signedIn.description:
True if whoever asked is signed in: the wizard starts at the sign-in until they are, whatever
 the installation already has.

development.title: development
development.description: True for a development installation, where the mock identity provider may be enabled.

volumesExist.title: volumes_exist
volumesExist.description:
Whether volumes exist, whose history is in this store: it can then be changed, but not
 for another bucket or directory.

unreferencedLayers.title: unreferenced_layers
unreferencedLayers.description: Layers no commit in the store names: the storage GC's to collect.

other.title: other
other.description: Everything outside volumes/ and layers/: the control plane's election records.

id.title: id
id.description: ID, path (e.g., "/engineering/backend") or "me": the caller's personal team

currentUserRole.title: current_user_role
currentUserRole.description: Role of the requesting user in this team

reportedAt.title: reported_at
reportedAt.description:
Unset: the watch has not reported since this control plane started - no collector, or not
 yet.

windowSeconds.title: window_seconds
windowSeconds.description: How long the counts below are over.

spans.title: spans
spans.description: Into the installation's store, after the traces policy chose which to keep.

samples.title: samples
samples.description: Into the installation's store of metrics.

traceId.title: trace_id
traceId.description: Hex, as a log record carries it.

unavailable.title: unavailable
unavailable.description:
Why this control plane cannot publish - no object store, or a build with no machine tools
 to make the image with - and empty when it can.

lines.title: lines
lines.description: How many lines from the end; zero asks for the default. The host bounds it either way.

lines.title: lines
lines.description: Newest last, as the console was written.

truncated.title: truncated
truncated.description:
truncated says there are lines before the first one here, so what this begins with is not
 mistaken for the start of the boot.

hostId.title: host_id
hostId.description:
Which host answered. A console belongs to the machine that wrote it, and a workspace that
 has moved has nothing to say about the run that failed on the host it left.

spin.v1.GetWorkspaceEgressRequest.title: GetWorkspaceEgressRequest
spin.v1.GetWorkspaceEgressRequest.description:
GetWorkspaceEgressRequest asks what a workspace has reached beyond the node. The host keeps
 the record, so the workspace has to be running on one; it is kept for six hours and survives
 a restart of the runner, not of the host.

destinations.title: destinations
destinations.description: Most traffic first, so what an allowlist has to carry is at the top.

lookups.title: lookups
lookups.description:
The workspace's recent lookups its host's resolver did not answer as asked, newest first:
 "it cannot resolve github.com" is an upstream failing, a name pointing into the node being
 removed, or a query type refused, and this says which. Answered lookups are not kept.

refused.title: refused
refused.description:
What the host's drops refused the workspace in the last hour, most packets first: the
 node's own networks, or what none of its policies allows. The other half of destinations,
 and what a policy that is too narrow looks like from outside the machine.

brokered.title: brokered
brokered.description:
The workspace's recent requests to names its policies broker with an injection, newest
 first: what the host's egress proxy set a header on, and what it refused and why. A brokered
 name no rule injects on is relayed byte for byte and leaves no request here.

spiffeId.title: spiffe_id
spiffeId.description:
The workspace's SPIFFE ID, spiffe://<domain>/t/<team>/w/<workspace>: every subject in it is
 under it - the user's at /u, each agent's at /a/<name> - so a relying party names the
 workspace by it as a prefix.

userSubject.title: user_subject
userSubject.description: The workspace user's subject, what its tokens and signatures carry.

issuer.title: issuer
issuer.description: The issuer its tokens name, https://id.<domain>, where the key set and the allowed signers are.

parentSnapshotId.title: parent_snapshot_id
parentSnapshotId.description:
What the workspace was cloned from: the snapshot, and the workspace whose disk it was when
 that is still there and of the same team. A workspace made from an image is cloned from the
 image's snapshot, and no workspace's: the snapshot is named and the workspace is empty.

audiences.title: audiences
audiences.description: Who the installation gives identities for; empty is anybody.

spin.v1.GetWorkspaceStatusRequest.title: GetWorkspaceStatusRequest
spin.v1.GetWorkspaceStatusRequest.description:
GetWorkspace is on the hot path - the proxy resolves every request through it - and
 serves one row; this joins four and is asked when something looks wrong.

state.title: state
state.description: What the control plane believes, which is what every other surface shows.

disagreements.title: disagreements
disagreements.description:
Where the four disagree, in the order they should be read. Empty means they agree -
 which is the answer when a workspace is simply healthy, and is worth saying.

runtime.title: runtime
runtime.description:
What the machine has and uses now, asked of its host. Absent - not zero - when there is no
 machine to ask about: not running, on no connected host, or a host that did not answer in
 time. Zero cores would read as a machine that has none.

failure.title: failure
failure.description: Which part failed, when state = FAILED; failure_reason is the detail. Workspace.failure.

injections.title: injections
injections.description:
Each header a brokered rule of the workspace's policies sets, and whether what it is set
 from is there to set: a request to a brokered name is refused when it is not, and this is
 where that is seen from outside the machine.

url.title: url
url.description: Where the control plane serves it: "/monitoring/grafana/".

dashboards.title: dashboards
dashboards.description: The release's, in the order they are listed.

spin.v1.Grafana.title: Grafana
spin.v1.Grafana.description:
Grafana is the one the control plane runs over the installation's metrics and serves to its
 administrators.

spin.v1.GrantPortAccessRequest.title: GrantPortAccessRequest
spin.v1.GrantPortAccessRequest.description:
Granting and revoking are separate from SetPortAccess because they answer a different
 question - who, rather than how many - and because revoking one person must not be
 expressible as "send the list again minus one", which loses a race with a second grant.

lasts.title: lasts
lasts.description:
How long the grant lasts before it is given back on its own, from now: at least a minute.
 Unset keeps it until it is given back. Each grant says it anew: one that says nothing about
 time is kept, whatever the one before it said.

move.title: move
move.description:
move says what to do when a running workspace's host has no room for the grant: move it to
 a host that has - suspended where it runs, its processes as they are, and resumed there from
 the checkpoint. The guest is paused from the checkpoint until it runs on the other host, which
 takes as long as storing its memory and publishing its disk. Without it such a grant is
 refused.

spin.v1.GrantWorkspaceResourcesRequest.title: GrantWorkspaceResourcesRequest
spin.v1.GrantWorkspaceResourcesRequest.description:
SetWorkspaceNetworkTagsRequest is the whole set a workspace should run under, not an
 addition: a request naming one tag leaves it carrying that one. Naming none means what it
 means on a create - the installation's default, and "offline" where it declares none - so
 there is one reading of an empty list rather than two nobody would keep straight. To ask for
 a workspace that reaches nothing, name "offline".

 Who may ask what: the workspace's owner chooses among the policies the installation
 declares, which are the same ones they could have created it with; an administrator may
 name any policy a host reports. Nothing inside the guest can ask at all - a workspace's own
 credential does not reach this, because loosening the egress of the sandbox you are in is
 the first thing something that got in would try.
 GrantWorkspaceResourcesRequest is what the workspace holds of its own from now on: at least its
 floor, and at most its ceiling where its preset has one (to_host has none but its host's room).
 Zero keeps what it holds of that one.

prefix.title: prefix
prefix.description: What goes before the value, as "Bearer ".

identity.title: identity
identity.description:
The audience of a token of the workspace's identity, issued for the proxy to present: bound
 to no key, and saying so (spin.via = egress-proxy).

forge.title: forge
forge.description:
The forge whose credential for the workspace's team goes in the header, whole: "github" is an
 installation token of the team's GitHub App, minted by the control plane (TeamService.SetForge).

methods.title: methods
methods.description:
The requests the header is set on: these methods, and paths under path_prefix by whole
 segments. Another request to the rule's names is answered 403. None of either is every request.

spin.v1.HeaderInjection.title: HeaderInjection
spin.v1.HeaderInjection.description:
HeaderInjection is a header the egress proxy sets: header, to prefix and then a value the
 workspace never holds - a team secret's, or a token of the workspace's identity. One of the two.

spin.v1.HealthReport.title: HealthReport
spin.v1.HealthReport.description:
HealthReport is what the supervisor inside a workspace observes about it. Here rather
 than beside the stream that carries it, for the reason SupervisorState is here: it is
 read from both sides - reported by the supervisor on its own connection
 (spin.agent.v1), and returned to an operator by WorkspaceService.GetWorkspaceStatus.

 It is also what keeps the dependency between the two packages pointing one way.
 spin.v1 is the vocabulary and spin.agent.v1 is the machine surface built on it; a type
 the operator's side needs from the agent's side would make each package need the other.

intervals.title: intervals
intervals.description:
How many intervals to split the window into: 1 to 200, 60 when unset. Each is at least a
 second.

lastHeartbeat.title: last_heartbeat
lastHeartbeat.description:
last_heartbeat is whichever of this host's two channels was heard from last, and they are
 not the same thing: the command stream carries what the host can be *told* (start this,
 stop that), and the volume agent's own heartbeat renews the lease its disks are served
 under. Either refreshes this, so a fresh stamp says one of them is alive and not which.

connected.title: connected
connected.description:
connected is the command stream, now: the half that decides whether this host can be given
 a workspace or asked to stop one. A host whose stream is gone while its volume agent keeps
 renewing reads as freshly heartbeated above and can be told nothing at all - which is the
 state an operator is looking at when they ask why a host takes no work.

goingAway.title: going_away
goingAway.description:
going_away is this host on its way out: a runner told the control plane it is stopping -
 an operator's restart, or the cloud taking the machine away - and it takes no new
 workspace from that moment. Nothing is written to the database for it (a state there would
 outlive the restart it described), so this is the only place an operator can see that the
 host they are looking at is leaving rather than idle.

checks.title: checks
checks.description:
checks are what the host last found when it asked itself whether a workspace can run on it
 as it should, as its heartbeat said: held for as long as the host is connected, like
 going_away, and empty for a host that has said nothing yet.

name.title: name
name.description: name is what was checked: clock, kvm, resolver.

detail.title: detail
detail.description: detail is what it found when it is not ok, in the host's words.

spin.v1.HostCheck.title: HostCheck
spin.v1.HostCheck.description:
HostCheck is one thing a host asks itself about, at start and every few minutes: a clock that
 is not synchronised, a KVM it cannot open, a resolver that answers its workspaces nothing - each
 a host that looks healthy to every other signal and fails its workspaces.

shutdownGraceSeconds.title: shutdown_grace_seconds
shutdownGraceSeconds.description:
Seconds this host stays up after a stop signal so what it runs can be suspended off it.
 The unit's TimeoutStopSec still bounds it.

preemptible.title: preemptible
preemptible.description: Whether a stop here is the machine being taken away rather than coming back.

preemptionSource.title: preemption_source
preemptionSource.description: Which cloud announces that reclaim; setting one implies preemptible.

preemptionMetadataUrl.title: preemption_metadata_url
preemptionMetadataUrl.description: That service's address, for a private cloud or a test.

capacityCpuCores.title: capacity_cpu_cores
capacityCpuCores.description:
What this host advertises to the fleet, which is not what it has: an operator holds a
 machine back by saying it has less. Unset leaves the host advertising what it detects.

maxWorkspaceCpuCores.title: max_workspace_cpu_cores
maxWorkspaceCpuCores.description: The ceiling one workspace may grow to here, for the machines it starts afterwards.

revision.title: revision
revision.description: revision names the content, and is what a host reports it is running under.

writebackLimitBytes.title: writeback_limit_bytes
writebackLimitBytes.description:
The host's writeback thresholds (spin.agent.v1.HostPolicy says why): both or neither, the
 background below the limit. Unset is what the host booted with.

runningRevision.title: running_revision
runningRevision.description:
running_revision is what the host last said, empty where it has not said or is not
 connected. Different from revision is a policy still on its way, which is normal for the
 seconds after a write and a fault after that.

maxWorkspaceIoMbPerSecond.title: max_workspace_io_mb_per_second
maxWorkspaceIoMbPerSecond.description:
What one machine may read and write per second here, in MiB and in operations, for the
 machines it starts afterwards. Unset is no bound.

spin.v1.HostPolicy.title: HostPolicy
spin.v1.HostPolicy.description:
HostPolicy is what an installation decides about one host. An unset field is the
 installation saying nothing about that setting, which leaves the host on its own default -
 not the same as setting it to nothing.

spin.v1.HostState.title: HostState
spin.v1.HostState.description:
HostState mirrors internal/lifecycle.HostState (§28.1) and the CHECK on hosts.state:
 one vocabulary for the fleet, whichever component is asking. Only ACTIVE takes new
 work; a CORDONED or DRAINING host keeps serving (and keeps its lease) while it is
 evacuated, and the Agent needs to be told which of the two it is.

 It replaces a second set of names this schema carried for the same states - HEALTHY,
 DEGRADED, OFFLINE - where DEGRADED was a word nothing branched on and no name said
 "an operator stopped this host".

spin.v1.IdentityProvider.title: IdentityProvider
spin.v1.IdentityProvider.description:
Identity provider info (returned to clients for login UI)
 Built-in provider has id="github"; dynamic providers have UUIDv7 IDs

ref.title: ref
ref.description:
The name a workspace asks for. It moves: a publish under it tags new bytes, and what a disk
 began as is its volume's parent snapshot, not this.

virtualSizeBytes.title: virtual_size_bytes
virtualSizeBytes.description: What the disk cloned from it will hold before the workspace writes anything.

publishedAt.title: published_at
publishedAt.description: When the publication this ref resolves to was made.

name.title: name
name.description:
What a person choosing a disk is shown: its name ("base image") and what it is ready for.
 An empty name is a publication made before one was asked for; show the ref.

spin.v1.Image.title: Image
spin.v1.Image.description:
Image is one name a workspace can be created from: a publication in this installation's
 database that its settings also permit. It is not a container image and does not come from a
 registry - it is a volume somebody published here, which is why a name that looks like
 "ubuntu:22.04" is not one unless it was published under that name.
 A disk image a workspace's disk can be cloned from: a volume published in this installation,
 not a container image, and never pulled from a registry.

policy.title: policy
policy.description: The policy, by name, and the names its rule brokers.

from.title: from
from.description:
What the header is set from: a team secret by name, "<forge> app", or "identity for
 <audience>".

held.title: held
held.description:
Whether the team holds it: the secret is set, the forge app is set, an identity is always
 held. False is a request refused with credentials.

spin.v1.InjectionStatus.title: InjectionStatus
spin.v1.InjectionStatus.description:
InjectionStatus is one header the egress proxy sets on the workspace's requests to a brokered
 name, and whether the workspace's team holds what it is set from.

allowedImages.title: allowed_images
allowedImages.description: Whitelist of allowed images (empty = all allowed)

defaultNetworkTags.title: default_network_tags
defaultNetworkTags.description:
What a workspace created without a network tag of its own runs under, by policy name.
 Empty means "offline", the policy every host has and which allows nothing: no value of
 this field means open. An installation that wants such a workspace out declares a policy
 saying what it may reach and names it here.

telemetryTracesKeepPercent.title: telemetry_traces_keep_percent
telemetryTracesKeepPercent.description:
What the installation's collector keeps, decided at the collector
 (internal/controlplane/domain/telemetrypolicy). A trace with an error in any span is always kept, and so
 is one slower than telemetry_traces_slow_ms (0: none is kept for being slow); of the rest,
 telemetry_traces_keep_percent, 0 to 100 and 100 until an admin says otherwise.

telemetryMetricsDrop.title: telemetry_metrics_drop
telemetryMetricsDrop.description: The metrics that are not kept, by name; a pattern may begin or end with *.

telemetryPerVolumeHistograms.title: telemetry_per_volume_histograms
telemetryPerVolumeHistograms.description:
Read only: the metrics that cost most to keep, a histogram per volume, which a surface may
 offer to drop as one.

vscodeFetch.title: vscode_fetch
vscodeFetch.description:
Whether the control plane fetches VS Code servers from Microsoft on its own: the newest
 stable release, looked for daily, and the server of a client's commit the installation has
 not released. False, it fetches none, and a workspace is given the server the control plane's
 image carries or one an administrator published.

workspaceTrashDays.title: workspace_trash_days
workspaceTrashDays.description:
How many days a deleted workspace stays in the trash, whole, for its owner to undelete
 before it is erased: 0 is no trash, and 7 is what an installation that says nothing keeps.

identityAudiences.title: identity_audiences
identityAudiences.description:
Who a workspace's identity token may be for; empty is anybody. What the installation's
 issuer gives, not who trusts it: a relying party still decides which subjects it admits.

volumeRpoSeconds.title: volume_rpo_seconds
volumeRpoSeconds.description:
How far behind the object store a workspace's volume may fall, in seconds, where its preset
 does not say: what it commits on (v6 §11). 0 is none - it commits on its size and its
 snapshots alone - and 300 is what an installation that says nothing keeps.

diskReservePercent.title: disk_reserve_percent
diskReservePercent.description:
How a host's disk is lent to workspaces. A volume holds what it wrote, not its size: a host
 is charged, per volume, the larger of disk_reserve_percent of its size and what it wrote,
 and takes new ones up to 80% of its device; disk_commit_max_percent bounds the sizes
 summed - every volume filling at once. 50 and 200 are what an installation that says
 nothing lends; 100 and 100 lends nothing past what the device holds.

workspaceIdleSuspendMinutes.title: workspace_idle_suspend_minutes
workspaceIdleSuspendMinutes.description:
How many minutes a running workspace may go unused - nobody working over its ssh, editor or
 forwarded ports, and its cores all but still - before it is suspended with its processes,
 which its next start resumes. 0 suspends none; 60 is what an installation that says nothing
 keeps, and a week is the most.

workspaceMaxRunningMinutes.title: workspace_max_running_minutes
workspaceMaxRunningMinutes.description:
How many minutes a workspace may run at a stretch, used or not, before it is suspended the
 same way: a process that keeps its cores busy is use to the rule above, and this is what
 ends it. Counted from its machine's start, which a resume is too. 0 caps none; 720 is what
 an installation that says nothing keeps, and a week is the most.

workspaceLeaseMaxMinutes.title: workspace_lease_max_minutes
workspaceLeaseMaxMinutes.description:
How many minutes a process may keep its workspace awake at a stretch (a lease:
 `spin-supervisor keep -- <cmd>`, a .spin.yaml task with keep_awake). While a lease is held
 and within this of its start, nobody is asked, nothing idle is suspended, and the running
 cap waits for the lease's end. 0 honours no lease; 480 is what an installation that says
 nothing keeps, and a week is the most.

teamSecretsRole.title: team_secrets_role
teamSecretsRole.description:
The IAM role a team's secret kept in Secrets Manager or Parameter Store is read under, in a
 session tagged spin-team-id with the team: its policy lets that session read only what carries
 the same tag. Empty, no secret is kept as a reference.

agentsFetch.title: agents_fetch
agentsFetch.description:
Whether the control plane fetches the agent CLIs - Claude Code and Codex - from their
 publishers on its own: the newest release of each, looked for daily. False, it fetches none,
 and a workspace is given the pair the control plane's image carries or one an administrator
 published.

spin.v1.InstallationSettings.title: InstallationSettings
spin.v1.InstallationSettings.description: InstallationSettings contains global settings for the Spin installation

intervalSeconds.title: interval_seconds
intervalSeconds.description: Zero for a job only run by hand, which has no next_run_at.

nextRunAt.title: next_run_at
nextRunAt.description: When the schedule next starts it.

lastRun.title: last_run
lastRun.description: Unset until it has run on this installation.

counts.title: counts
counts.description: What it did, by the job's own names for it: objects deleted, bytes freed, hosts forgotten.

error.title: error
error.description: Why it failed; empty when it did not.

traceId.title: trace_id
traceId.description: The run's trace, empty when it was not recorded.

askedBy.title: asked_by
askedBy.description: The admin who ran it by hand; empty for a run the schedule started.

spin.v1.JobRunOutcome.title: JobRunOutcome
spin.v1.JobRunOutcome.description: How one run of a job ended, or that it has not.

lasts.title: lasts
lasts.description: How long from now it is kept awake: a minute to a day.

actorId.title: actor_id
actorId.description:
Each filter is optional and they are combined with AND; an empty request is the whole
 log, newest first.

since.title: since
since.description:
since bounds the listing at the older end; an audit log is read forward from an
 incident, and the whole of one is not what a page wants.

actions.title: actions
actions.description:
actions and resource_types are every value this installation can record, so a reader
 building a filter does not have to know them. They come from the code rather than from
 a DISTINCT over the log: the log is the one table that only grows, and a vocabulary
 that is empty until something happens is a filter that is empty when it matters.

totalCapped.title: total_capped
totalCapped.description:
total_capped says page.total_count is where counting stopped, not the count: the log is
 counted up to a bound, since counting all of it is reading all of it on every page.

spin.v1.ListIdentityProvidersRequest.title: ListIdentityProvidersRequest
spin.v1.ListIdentityProvidersRequest.description: Not paginated: the login page offers every enabled provider, a set an admin configures.

images.title: images
images.description: One entry per name, newest publication of it, in the order a person reads a list.

limit.title: limit
limit.description: At most this many, newest first; zero is the default of 50.

hostsEnforcing.title: hosts_enforcing
hostsEnforcing.description:
Of the hosts connected, how many have installed what the installation declares. They are
 told on their next heartbeat, so the two differ for a moment after an apply - and go on
 differing when a host cannot install what was declared, which is the thing worth seeing.

includePublic.title: include_public
includePublic.description: false: only what was shared with the caller

outsideTeam.title: outside_team
outsideTeam.description:
outside_team is the snapshot's share outside its team: what a clone by somebody of another
 team stands on, made when the snapshot is first shared outside the team or made public. A
 clone of it outside the team is refused until it is ready.

baseSnapshotId.title: base_snapshot_id
baseSnapshotId.description:
What the workspace's disk is cloned from now: the snapshot last restored to, or the one it
 was cloned from - for a workspace made from an image, that image's. Empty for a disk that was
 not cloned.

parentId.title: parent_id
parentId.description: Optional: filter by parent (empty = root teams only)

includeAllDescendants.title: include_all_descendants
includeAllDescendants.description: If true, include all nested teams

everyTeam.title: every_team
everyTeam.description:
every_team lists the whole installation rather than the caller's own teams - the
 administration view, and only an instance admin may ask for it. It is asked for rather
 than inferred from who is calling: an admin's own Teams page should be their teams, not
 a list of everybody's personal team that they cannot get out of.

query.title: query
query.description: Optional: filter by name or email

limit.title: limit
limit.description: How many of the newest to answer; the newest first.

teamId.title: team_id
teamId.description: Optional filter by team (empty = all user's workspaces)

retention.title: retention
retention.description: How long it keeps what it holds, in the store's words ("30 days"); empty for forever.

timestampField.title: timestamp_field
timestampField.description: The field its records are dated by: what a search's window is over.

defaultSearchFields.title: default_search_fields
defaultSearchFields.description: What a query's bare words are searched in.

documents.title: documents
documents.description:
What it holds: records, the splits they are kept in, and the splits' size in the bucket
 and the records' before compression.

oldest.title: oldest
oldest.description: When its oldest and newest records are dated; unset while it holds none.

spin.v1.LogIndex.title: LogIndex
spin.v1.LogIndex.description: LogIndex is one index of the store.

name.title: name
name.description: A dotted path for a field inside an object field.

type.title: type
type.description: The store's type: text, json, u64, bool, bytes, datetime, array<text>...

tokenizer.title: tokenizer
tokenizer.description:
How a text or JSON field is split into what a query matches: "raw" is the whole value as
 written, "default" is its words, lowercased. Empty for any other type.

indexed.title: indexed
indexed.description: Whether a query can match it, and whether it can be counted and ranged over fast.

spin.v1.LogIndexField.title: LogIndexField
spin.v1.LogIndexField.description: LogIndexField is one field of an index's mapping.

spin.v1.LogInterval.title: LogInterval
spin.v1.LogInterval.description: LogInterval is how many records one interval holds, by severity.

service.title: service
service.description: The process that wrote it: controlplane, runner, proxy.

body.title: body
body.description: What was logged: its message, or the structure it logged.

traceId.title: trace_id
traceId.description: The trace it was written in, hex; empty for none.

spin.v1.LogRecord.title: LogRecord
spin.v1.LogRecord.description: LogRecord is one record as OpenTelemetry names its parts.

hosts.title: hosts
hosts.description: What each host reporting this tag says it enforces.

declared.title: declared
declared.description:
declared says the installation has this policy, and rules are what it allows. A policy with
 no hosts is declared and not yet enforced anywhere.

teamId.title: team_id
teamId.description:
The team whose admins declared it, which only its workspaces and those of the teams below
 it may run under; empty is the installation's.

spin.v1.NetworkPolicy.title: NetworkPolicy
spin.v1.NetworkPolicy.description:
NetworkPolicy is a tag a workspace can be created with, and what the hosts reporting it say
 it allows. The hosts are the authority: this is what they last said they enforce.

spin.v1.NetworkPolicyRule.title: NetworkPolicyRule
spin.v1.NetworkPolicyRule.description:
NetworkPolicyRule is a policy as an administrator writes it, in the words the config file
 takes: a name, which is a tag - letters, digits, - and _, up to 32 - and the rules it allows,
 each these destinations on these ports. A policy with no rules allows nothing.

allowNames.title: allow_names
allowNames.description:
Names, exact or with a leading "*.": the host opens the address its own resolver answers a
 machine with, for as long as the answer lives.

ports.title: ports
ports.description:
Destination ports as "443" (TCP, which is what a bare number means), "443/udp", a range as
 "8000-8100" or "8000-8100/udp", or "icmp" for a ping. None is every port, at the
 destinations above; none of those is every destination, on these ports.

broker.title: broker
broker.description:
The host's egress proxy stands in for these names, on HTTPS only: a machine reaches them
 through it and never directly, and it adds what the machine never holds. Names only.

inject.title: inject
inject.description:
Headers the proxy sets on a brokered rule's requests, each from a secret of the workspace's
 team (or the nearest team above it with one by that name). Brokered rules only.

cloud.title: cloud
cloud.description:
The principal the proxy authorizes a brokered rule's requests as, on its cloud: the host takes
 its credentials as the workspace, with a token of its identity. Brokered rules naming that
 cloud's endpoints only, and not with inject.

verifySni.title: verify_sni
verifySni.description:
The host's egress proxy reads the TLS server name of each connection to these names and passes
 on, untouched, only one this rule names: an address shared with other names opens only these
 to a client that says which it wants. A connection with no name, or one hiding it (ECH), goes
 nowhere. Names only, on TCP, never with broker; it does not stop a client that lies.

principal.title: principal
principal.description:
Whose connections a brokered rule stands in for: "agent" (the workspace's agent, whose packets
 its guest marks), "user" (everything else the workspace sends), or "any" (empty: both). Two
 rules for one name, one per principal, each with its own injections and methods, say what the
 person may do and what the agent may. Brokered rules only: an agent reaches nothing outside
 the proxy, so a rule that is not brokered is the person's already.

spin.v1.NetworkRule.title: NetworkRule
spin.v1.NetworkRule.description:
NetworkRule is one thing a network policy allows: these destinations on these ports. Within a
 rule the two intersect - every destination on every port - and a policy is the union of its
 rules, so "53/udp to one resolver and 443 to github.com" is two rules and not a product of
 both. Here and not beside a policy for the reason HealthReport is: the control plane's policy,
 the one a host reports it enforces and the one a host is given are one vocabulary.

packets.title: packets
packets.description: What the workspace sent there, every packet of every flow.

port.title: port
port.description: For tcp and udp; zero otherwise.

packetsReceived.title: packets_received
packetsReceived.description: What came back to the workspace from there.

spin.v1.ObservedDestination.title: ObservedDestination
spin.v1.ObservedDestination.description:
ObservedDestination is one address the workspace was allowed to reach, with what the host's
 ruleset counted and the name its resolver answered with that address, where it holds one.

workspaceName.title: workspace_name
workspaceName.description: From the subdomain, as CheckPortAccess takes it

port.title: port
port.description: The published port inside the workspace

sessionToken.title: session_token
sessionToken.description:
The session token of whoever the connection is being opened for, validated here.

 It is the difference between a control plane that can refuse and one that cannot. The
 proxy gates each request in front, but this is reachable on its own, and without a
 credential to check, anything that could reach it would open a session into any
 published port of any workspace. Empty is allowed and reaches only PUBLIC ports.

httpsBackend.title: https_backend
httpsBackend.description: The hostname's s. A port whose flag differs answers as one that is not exposed.

workspaceId.title: workspace_id
workspaceId.description:
The workspace CheckPortAccess decided the request about. A name that now names another
 answers as a port that is not exposed: the session is for the workspace that was decided.

spin.v1.OpenWorkspaceProxySessionRequest.title: OpenWorkspaceProxySessionRequest
spin.v1.OpenWorkspaceProxySessionRequest.description:
Opening one connection into a published port, for the proxy.

 Separate from CheckPortAccess, which the proxy calls on every request to decide whether the
 browser may reach the port. This one is called only when a new connection is actually
 needed - http.Transport pools them, so a page of fifty assets opens a handful - and each
 call costs a command to the workspace's runner.

 The authorization is the same question CheckPortAccess answers and is asked again here
 rather than carried over: a session is a way into somebody's workspace, and the decision to
 open one belongs beside the opening.

relayUrl.title: relay_url
relayUrl.description:
Where the two ends of this connection meet, and the token that names it there. Set only
 when status is ACCESSIBLE. The token is single-use: one connection, one token.

httpsBackend.title: https_backend
httpsBackend.description: The flag of the row the session was authorized on: whether the proxy speaks TLS.

spin.v1.OutsideShareState.title: OutsideShareState
spin.v1.OutsideShareState.description:
OutsideShareState is how far a snapshot's share outside its team is.

- `OUTSIDE_SHARE_STATE_UNSPECIFIED`: None: the snapshot was never shared outside its team, nor made public.
- `OUTSIDE_SHARE_STATE_PREPARING`: A host is writing the keys a clone outside the team reads the snapshot with.
- `OUTSIDE_SHARE_STATE_READY`: Somebody of another team can create a workspace from it.
x-enum-descriptions: None: the snapshot was never shared outside its team, nor made public.
A host is writing the keys a clone outside the team reads the snapshot with.
Somebody of another team can create a workspace from it.

spin.v1.OwnerWord.title: OwnerWord
spin.v1.OwnerWord.description:
OwnerWord is a workspace's access, as its owner signed it with a key of their keyring
 (internal/ownerword): document is the access as framed JSON, signature the key's SSH signature
 over it (sshsig, namespace "spin-access") - what `ssh-keygen -Y sign` writes, so a FIDO2 key
 signs one through ssh-agent.

forcePasswordChange.title: force_password_change
forcePasswordChange.description: True if user must change password before proceeding

subjectId.title: subject_id
subjectId.description: subject_id is the user, the team or the workspace the document is of.

document.title: document
document.description: document is the document to sign, as framed JSON: what the client shows and signs as it is.

signers.title: signers
signers.description: signers are the keys, in authorized_keys form, any one of which may sign it.

summary.title: summary
summary.description: summary is a line saying what it changes, for a list: the document itself is what to read.

spin.v1.PendingSignature.title: PendingSignature
spin.v1.PendingSignature.description: PendingSignature is one document the caller is asked to sign.

detail.title: detail
detail.description: Why it failed, or why it is left alone.

version.title: version
version.description: The machine's release, or the supervisor's (the control plane's) version.

spin.v1.PlatformImageArtifact.title: PlatformImageArtifact
spin.v1.PlatformImageArtifact.description:
- `PLATFORM_IMAGE_ARTIFACT_BASE`: The machine's base image, every workspace's disk's floor.
- `PLATFORM_IMAGE_ARTIFACT_SUPERVISOR`: The supervisor extension every workspace is handed.
x-enum-descriptions: The machine's base image, every workspace's disk's floor.
The supervisor extension every workspace is handed.

spin.v1.PlatformImageState.title: PlatformImageState
spin.v1.PlatformImageState.description:
- `PLATFORM_IMAGE_STATE_UNAVAILABLE`: This build carries nothing to publish.
- `PLATFORM_IMAGE_STATE_FOREIGN`: The ref names an image somebody else published, which is left as it is.
x-enum-descriptions: This build carries nothing to publish.
The ref names an image somebody else published, which is left as it is.

limit.title: limit
limit.description: How many values, the commonest first: 1 to 100, 10 when unset.

other.title: other
other.description: How many records the search found with a value not among these.

spin.v1.PortAccess.title: PortAccess
spin.v1.PortAccess.description:
Who may reach a published port.

 Per port rather than per workspace: one workspace serves a demo anyone may see and an
 admin panel only its owner may, and a single setting for both makes the safe answer for
 one the wrong answer for the other.

 UNSPECIFIED is not a level and is never stored - the column's CHECK excludes it. A
 request that leaves it at proto3's zero is treated as PRIVATE, which is the direction to
 be wrong in: the cost of failing closed is a confusing error, and the cost of failing
 open is a port somebody published without meaning to.

- `PORT_ACCESS_PRIVATE`: Only the workspace's owner, who must be signed in.
- `PORT_ACCESS_WHITELIST`: The owner, and the users the owner granted. See GrantPortAccess.
- `PORT_ACCESS_PUBLIC`: Anyone, with no session at all. Nothing is asked and nobody is redirected to a login.
  Until the workspace stops or fails: then the port is PRIVATE again, and made public again
  when it is meant to be.
x-enum-descriptions: Only the workspace's owner, who must be signed in.
The owner, and the users the owner granted. See GrantPortAccess.

Anyone, with no session at all. Nothing is asked and nobody is redirected to a login.
 Until the workspace stops or fails: then the port is PRIVATE again, and made public again
 when it is meant to be.

email.title: email
email.description: Output only, so a list is readable without a second lookup

spin.v1.PortGrant.title: PortGrant
spin.v1.PortGrant.description: One user a whitelisted port is shared with.

parentId.title: parent_id
parentId.description: The prebuild it was built on, and how many builds it is from the image (0: built from it).

settingsDigest.title: settings_digest
settingsDigest.description: The SHA-256 of the settings its word approved, and of the checkout's .spin.yaml at the commit.

claim.title: claim

spin.v1.RecoverWorkspaceRequest.title: RecoverWorkspaceRequest
spin.v1.RecoverWorkspaceRequest.description:
Recovering a workspace whose host is gone.

 StartWorkspace requires the host the workspace was placed on and refuses while it is not
 connected, so a workspace on a host that died cannot be started again - there is no
 amount of waiting or retrying that fixes it. Recovering re-homes it: the volume is taken
 from the dead host and placed on a live one, and the workspace becomes startable.

 The cost is everything the dead host had written and not yet published, and that cost is
 the owner's to accept rather than an operator's to impose - which is why this is an RPC
 of theirs. Called without accept_data_loss it reports the cost and changes nothing; the
 same call with it does the work.

 It is not automatic. A host wrongly believed dead, recovered from, is two machines
 writing one disk - which is the failure the whole lease exists to prevent. The safety is
 not in the confirmation, though: taking the volume goes through the same check an
 operator's -detach-volume does, and is refused unless the old host has been *observed* to
 have stopped. The confirmation is about the data, not about the fencing.

spin.v1.WaitWorkspaceRequest.title: WaitWorkspaceRequest
spin.v1.WaitWorkspaceRequest.description:
A workspace's state is held by four parties that can disagree, and the disagreement is
 the diagnosis. The control plane has a lifecycle state it set; the supervisor inside the
 guest reports what it is doing and how it is; the host either heartbeats or does not; the
 volume either serves the disk or refuses with a reason. Asking any one of them alone
 produces the two failures this answers: a workspace the control plane calls RUNNING whose
 supervisor stopped reporting ten minutes ago, and one that looks broken because its host
 is unreachable, which is a different repair.

 It is its own RPC and not fields on GetWorkspace because those are different questions.
 WaitWorkspaceRequest names the state to wait for: RUNNING or STOPPED.

 Answered with the workspace once it is in that state. Refused as soon as waiting cannot end
 there: FAILED_PRECONDITION with the failure reason when the workspace failed, or when it is
 neither in that state nor wanted in it (a stop was asked for while waiting for RUNNING).
 DEADLINE_EXCEEDED when timeout_seconds pass first.

 correcting it: RUNNING is not transitional, so nothing fails it and nothing moves it, and
 a workspace whose machine died with its host reads as healthy for ever. The honest answer
 is not a different state - a host that cannot be reached may be running the machine
 perfectly well behind a broken network - but to say that the state is old and why.

 False for a workspace with no host at all (a stopped one), so read it beside the state.

spin.v1.WorkspaceFailure.title: WorkspaceFailure
spin.v1.WorkspaceFailure.description:
WorkspaceFailure is why a FAILED workspace failed: which part of its run, closed so what a
 person can do about it - and a failure rate split by the repair it needs - is decided by the
 kind rather than by the text of an error. The reason beside it is the detail.

 One enum for the client and the host's report (spin.agent.v1.ObservedWorkspace): the kind a
 person is shown is the one the host named, with no second list to keep in step.

- `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_UNSPECIFIED`: Not classified. A failure that lands here is a site missing its classification.
- `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_VOLUME`: Its disk could not be served or made: the host is not serving its volume (its refusal says
  why), or what the disk was to be made from is gone.
- `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_EXTENSION`: An extension could not be attached, or the releases it starts with could not be named.
- `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_NETWORK`: The machine's network namespace or its tags could not be set up.
- `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_RESOURCES`: The machine could not be given the cores or memory it was asked for.
- `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_MACHINE`: QEMU could not be prepared or did not boot.
- `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_GUEST`: The guest booted and did not take its identity or its own filesystem.
- `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_RELEASE_GONE`: A resume needs an extension release that is no longer in the object store: the memory
  cannot be resumed anywhere, and the control plane boots the disk with the newest releases.
- `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_EXITED`: The machine ended without being asked to: its guest powered off, or its QEMU crashed or was
  killed.
- `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_STOP`: The machine could not be stopped or removed.
- `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_TIMED_OUT`: Its host did not bring a start or a stop to an end before the deadline: unreachable, or its
  attempts outlasted it. The control plane's verdict (the stuck sweep), never a host's.
- `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_NO_HOST`: No host could take it: none came with room while it waited, or its disk is only on a host
  that is not connected. The control plane's verdict, never a host's.
- `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_MACHINE_CHANGED`: Its memory was taken on a machine no host of the installation runs now: the machine's
  contract moved (a release that changed it), or the processor did. The memory resumes nowhere;
  the workspace stays suspended, and booting it from its disk, which drops the memory, is its
  owner's to choose (StartWorkspaceRequest.from_disk).

spin.v1.WorkspaceRuntime.description:
WorkspaceRuntime is a running workspace's machine as its host measures it from outside the
 guest. Answers "is my workspace out of memory" and "did it get the cores it borrowed" for the

spin.v1.WorkspaceState.title: WorkspaceState
spin.v1.WorkspaceState.description:
WorkspaceState is where a workspace is in its life. Each value's comment is what the API's
 document says of it (buf.gen.openapi.yaml's with-enum-value-descriptions), and the website's
 table of states is generated from it: it is written for a person reading that table, in the
 site's words (a runner, the CLI's commands). Why a value is what it is goes in a comment
 apart, above the value's own, which the document does not carry.

- `WORKSPACE_STATE_UNSPECIFIED`: Never a workspace's state: a client that reads it read a field nothing set.
- `WORKSPACE_STATE_CREATING`: The workspace exists and has not run yet.
- `WORKSPACE_STATE_STARTING`: A runner is preparing its disk and starting its machine.
- `WORKSPACE_STATE_RUNNING`: Its machine is up.
- `WORKSPACE_STATE_STOPPING`: Its machine is shutting down, and then what its disk wrote since its last commit is
  uploaded to the bucket. A stop stays here until the upload is done, and says why it is not;
  `spin workspace stop --force` does not wait for it.
- `WORKSPACE_STATE_STOPPED`: Not running. Its disk is kept, and the next start boots from it.
- `WORKSPACE_STATE_FAILED`: A start or a stop failed: `spin workspace status` says which part, and why. It stays so
  until it is started again.
- `WORKSPACE_STATE_DELETED`: In the trash, with its disk, for the days the installation keeps it there
  (`workspace_trash_days`): `spin workspace undelete` brings it back, stopped. An installation
  that keeps no trash erases it at once.
- `WORKSPACE_STATE_WAITING`: Wanted running, and no runner has room for it yet. On AWS, where runners scale to none, one
  is being started, and the workspace starts on it once it is up.
- `WORKSPACE_STATE_QUARANTINED`: Held by an administrator with `spin workspace quarantine`: it cannot start until
  `spin workspace unquarantine` releases it, and its disk is kept as it was.

tags.description:
SignatureService is what only people sign of themselves: who a user's keys are and who a team's
 members are. A host holds every workspace's access to these (internal/roster), so a control
 plane that is taken can say neither which keys are somebody's nor who is in a team. A
 workspace's access is signed through WorkspaceService.SetOwnerWord.

 The control plane proposes each document from what it holds - a key registered, a member added -
 and keeps what was signed; it signs nothing. A client shows a person what they are signing and
 signs it with a key of theirs: `spin sign`, with the keys ssh-agent holds, or the terminal's
 page, with a passkey.

 nothing on its own - only a key the owner's word for a workspace lists does, there.
